title: This startup is paying employees to post on LinkedIn
tldr: A startup is directly incentivizing employees to become LinkedIn creators, formalizing employee-generated content as a growth channel. A concrete look at how EGC gets operationalized (and its risks).
angle: When you pay staff to post: designing an employee-generated content program that stays authentic and doesn't backfire.

title: Конец идеальных фото: почему мы устали от фильтров и ретуши
tldr: Explores the shift toward unretouched, 'real' imagery on social platforms and why audiences crave authenticity over polish. Directly speaks to human-centered content and media-consumption shifts.
angle: The de-polishing of content: why 'people over perfection' is becoming a brand mandate.

title: Stop Marketing Like a Faceless Company. One Founder-Led Content Strategy Is Changing How Brands Grow
tldr: Makes the case for founder-led, human-fronted content as the differentiator in a faceless, AI-saturated feed. Practical framing on humanity in brand content.
angle: Faces beat logos: building a founder-led content engine without it collapsing when the founder leaves.

title: Marketers bemoan the culture of 'good enough' as standards fall amid the AI bubble
tldr: Marketers warn that AI is dragging content quality down to 'good enough,' splitting the internet into two audiences. A sharp read on craft erosion and the human-quality premium.
angle: The 'good enough' trap: why raising your content quality bar is now a competitive moat.

title: Beauty brands were writing AI slop before AI: how Uncommon won a D&AD Black Pencil for calling it out
tldr: Nils Leonard breaks down how painstaking craft turned buzzword parody into an award-winning campaign. A concrete campaign breakdown on craft vs. slop.
angle: Anti-slop as a creative strategy: what Uncommon's craft-first campaign teaches about standing out.

title: The most valuable thing AI can do for media isn't save time
tldr: Argues AI's real value in media isn't efficiency but enabling entirely new formats and experiences. A reframe worth stealing for content strategists.
angle: Beyond efficiency: using AI to create content you couldn't make before, not just faster.

title: How to break through social media saturation in a world of overwhelm
tldr: Argues against content-for-content's-sake and for meaning amid doom-scroll fatigue. Ties directly to how people consume media now.
angle: Content minimalism: doing less but landing harder in a saturated feed.

title: Here's what employees really need during any change
tldr: A comms leader shares how she keeps internal messaging simple through mergers, restructurings and rebrands. Practical change-communications playbook.
angle: Simplicity as a change-comms superpower: the messaging discipline that survives a merger.

title: Inside the creator economy's AI reckoning
tldr: Creators have swung from AI suspicion to treating it as necessary strategy. Useful pulse-check on how the creator economy is absorbing AI.
angle: From suspicion to survival: how creators are rationalizing AI without losing their audience's trust.

title: Qobuz Rolls Out Tags to Flag AI-Generated Music: 'Musical Discovery Must Remain Guided by Human Choices'
tldr: A streaming platform is labeling AI-generated music to protect human curation. A signal of the coming human-vs-synthetic labeling wave across content.
angle: The rise of 'human-made' labels: what content and brand teams should learn from AI-flagging on platforms.

title: Microsoft puts Brad Smith in charge of communications
tldr: Microsoft moves comms out of marketing and into legal/external affairs under Brad Smith. A telling structural signal about where corporate comms is heading.
angle: When comms reports to legal, not marketing: what Microsoft's reshuffle says about the function's future.

title: Reddit Is Ramping up Its War on Marketing Slop
tldr: Reddit is cracking down on low-effort marketing content to protect community trust. Relevant to owned/earned strategy on community platforms.
angle: Community platforms are policing brands: how to show up on Reddit without getting flagged as slop.

title: B2B Marketers Discover Buyers Are Human, Create A Framework
tldr: A new framework leans into the obvious-but-ignored truth that B2B buyers are people. Feeds the human-centered content thesis for B2B.
angle: Humanizing B2B: turning the 'buyers are people' cliché into an actual content operating model.

title: How Facebook's News Feed introduced the age of the algorithm 20 years ago
tldr: A retrospective on how the News Feed reshaped how billions consume media. Useful long-view context for media-consumption writing.
angle: 20 years of the feed: what the algorithm era teaches about designing for how people actually consume content.

title: What makes for a great brand partnership
tldr: Uses a Macy's Thanksgiving Parade collab to show partnerships work when each brand offers what the other can't credibly claim. Concrete collaboration breakdown.
angle: Credibility swap: the one question that separates strong brand partnerships from empty logo mashups.
